_comment: Greg's bench. COM numbers are this PC's. Wires are NOT listed here — they are auto-detected (GUI or run.py --discover) and saved to results/links.json. wiring_plan says which probe each WCB's ports should go to; taps are listen-only wires onto a line a real device already uses.

probe3.note: V2.4 board on NaviCore's own pins (D-NC37), formerly a WCB 6.2.0; wcb_probe 7

probe4.note: V2.4 board on WCB3's ports; wcb_probe 7

taps.why: Real Maestro 2 is on this port — the probe only listens, so the Maestro keeps working.
A real Kyber's Maestro port (115200, ?KYBER,LOCAL,S2): the probe only listens to what W3 sends back to it.

device_links.label: SBUS A: controller to NaviCore
device_links.signal: SBUS-24 (36-byte frames every 9 ms, ~111/s), 100 kbaud 8E2, inverted, 3.3 V. The controls ride it unless the controller is routed to the Kyber.
device_links.how: SBUS controller S5 TX (GPIO9) to NaviCore's SBUS IN signal pin (GPIO4, UART1 RX, shared with SBUS OUT on GPIO5), plus GND to GND. Signal only: no 5V between them, each board has its own supply.
device_links.check: NaviCore #L09 must read fps ~107-111, variant=SBUS-24, lost=no, failsafe=no. fps 0: the signal wire or GND, the controller unpowered or rebooting (its USB console), or the stream stopped by a test ({"t":"flags"} answers stream:false - SbusCtl.clear_faults() puts it back). Steady but nothing moves: the controller routed to the Kyber (the reply's "route" is not navicore). lost/failsafe=YES: a test left the flags byte set (clear_faults). variant SBUS-16: the frame format was changed (the controller's 'm' key or a "mode" verb).

device_links.label: SBUS B: controller to Kyber
device_links.signal: The same SBUS-24 as output A, but silent until the controller is routed to the Kyber ({"t":"route","to":"kyber"} or "both", RAM only; a reset gives navicore). The Kyber's pad buttons are CH7: Released 991, buttons 1-10 at 176-788 (tests/hil/kyber/bench_kyber_config.json).
device_links.how: SBUS controller S4 TX (GPIO17, formerly RC PWM output 4) to the Kyber's SBUS input signal pin, plus GND to GND. No 5V: the Kyber has its own supply.
device_links.check: Nothing reaches the Kyber unless routed: the controller's test reply must say route kyber or both. With it routed, the Kyber Config Editor's live calibration (RC Channels & Banks / Button Values) shows CH7 moving; resting it reads Released (991). Nothing there: the wire to S4 (not S5), GND, the controller image (fwver ...-eb0517a-hil or later, kyber-sbus branch). Buttons fire wrongly: the Kyber's _buttonsCH must be 7 and its Button Values the CH7 ladder.

device_links.label: Kyber Maestro port to WCB3 S2
device_links.signal: Pololu Maestro protocol, 115200 8N1 (Kyber Expert > Maestro must be 115200). The Kyber's TX is 5 V; WCB3's pins are 3.3 V (run direct on this bench; a BSS138 shifter or 1k/2k divider is the conservative option).
device_links.how: Kyber Maestro TX to WCB3 S2 RX (GPIO7), Kyber Maestro RX to WCB3 S2 TX (GPIO6), GND to GND. On WCB3: ?KYBER,LOCAL,S2 then ?reboot (the command does not reboot). Probe 4 header S2 may tap WCB3 S2's TX line (listen only).
device_links.check: On WCB3's console: ?KYBER,LIST shows Kyber local on S2; ?DEBUG,KYBER,ON dumps every bridged frame - press a Kyber Maestro button (CH7 176 = Maestro 1-1) and a frame must print. None: TX/RX swapped (swap them), GND, the Kyber's Maestro baud, WCB3 not rebooted after ?KYBER,LOCAL. Frames print but no servo moves: W1/W2 must be in Maestro-remote mode (?MAESTRO,REMOTE) and Maestro 2 wired (its own connection).

device_links.label: Kyber MarcDuino out to WCB3 S5
device_links.signal: MarcDuino-style text lines ending in CR, 9600 8N1, Kyber to WCB only. 5 V from the Kyber (see the Maestro port).
device_links.how: Kyber MarcDuino/serial TX to WCB3 S5 RX (GPIO10), GND to GND. WCB3's TX on S5 (GPIO9) stays unconnected. WCB3 S5 at ?BAUD,S5,9600 with broadcasts in on (the default).
device_links.check: Press Kyber button 7 (CH7 584, 'Periscope Up'): WCB3 runs ;w2;s4:PP100 and W2 S4 outputs :PP100 (probe 2 header S4 sees it). Nothing on WCB3's console: the wire to S5 RX (GPIO10, not 9), GND, ?BAUD,S5 not 9600, the Kyber's serial command output off (_serialSupport must be 1) or its baud not 9600.

device_links.label: Maestro 2 on WCB2 S1
device_links.signal: Pololu Maestro protocol, 115200 8N1 (WCB2's ?BAUD,S1). The real servos of the bench. Probe 2 header S2 listens to WCB2 S1's TX (a tap).
device_links.how: WCB2 S1 TX (GPIO8) to the Maestro's RX, the Maestro's TX to WCB2 S1 RX (GPIO21), GND to GND. Probe 2 header S2: GND and its RX pin on WCB2 S1's TX line only.
device_links.check: From W1: ;W2,;M2,getErrors must reach the Maestro (the probe tap sees AA 02 21) and its 2-byte reply come back (kyber.remote_roundtrip). No reply: the Maestro's TX to WCB2 RX, its serial mode (UART, fixed or detect baud 115200), its power. A servo that will not move: the Maestro's servo power (separate from its logic power), or ?MAESTRO slot M2 missing on WCB2.

device_links.label: NaviCore Maestro bus to the dome's Maestro 1
device_links.signal: Pololu Maestro protocol on NaviCore's Serial2, GET_CONFIG auxBaud.maestro (57600 on this bench). Probe 3 header S5 taps NaviCore's TX on it once wired (N20MAE).
device_links.how: NaviCore J3 Maestro TX (GPIO6) to the Maestro's RX, the Maestro's TX to NaviCore's Maestro RX (GPIO7, optional: only replies), GND to GND. J3 runs GND, 5V, RX, TX.
device_links.check: NaviCore ?MAE,GET,<slot>,0 must answer (navicore.bench_health). No answer: the Maestro's TX to GPIO7, the baud (auxBaud.maestro against the Maestro's own), power. Moves but no readback: only the reply line (GPIO7) is missing.
